commands.name: status
commands.description: Read-only snapshot: onboarding health, phase, gates, handoff, cell counts, reservations, active workers, decisions, staleness warnings, recommended next step. `lanes` is summarized by default: the ACTIVE lane (the one this session is bound to) in full, plus counts-by-phase and bare ids for every other lane record — pass --lanes-full for the full per-lane array. `workers` is a derived view — live-heartbeat sessions joined with their current cell claim — never state.json's hand-mutated `workers` array. `cells.archivable` is the retirement backlog — {features, cells, ids} for features whose cells are ALL terminal and which are therefore parsed on every call for nothing. `bee close` retires what it closes, so this only ever counts work that never went through close; the text report names it once it is worth a command.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text report.

lanes-full.description: Restore the `lanes` field to its full per-lane array (every lane record in full, including bound_sessions) instead of the default summary ({active, counts, ids}). Payload-size only — every other top-level field (phase/mode/feature/gates/cells/recommended_next/...) is unaffected either way.

brief.description: Fast orientation path for worker startup. Reads ONLY the state layer (state.json + config-derived gate_bypass_level/ship_visibility) — no cell scan, no review/handoff resolution, no models/tier_mix. Emits exactly {phase, feature, mode, gates, gate_bypass_level, ship_visibility, route} (route null when absent); ignored together with --lanes-full (mutually exclusive fast/full paths — --brief wins). Full `status` (this flag omitted) is unchanged.

commands.name: orient
commands.description: Session-start context packet: where the work is ({phase, feature, mode, gates, gate_bypass_level}), the decisions in force (active count, up to 3 recent one-liners, the feature's CONTEXT.md path when one exists on disk), the work state (open/claimed/capped counts, up to 5 ready cell ids, blockers), and exactly one recommended next step ({action, skill, command}) — the skill to load for the current phase, and a runnable command when the action names one (null otherwise). Reshapes the same snapshot `bee status` builds, plus ONE write of its own (sweep-at-every-door D1/D6): before the report is built, it resolves its own caller session and releases any OTHER session's expired, heartbeat-stale claim, parking that claim's cell `blocked` and naming the dead session and its worktree in the reason — the SAME sweep `bee cells claim-next` already runs, reached from a second door. When orient cannot resolve its own caller session it writes nothing and reports the count of expired claims it detected instead. `bee status` runs no such sweep and stays read-only.

json.description: Emit the machine-readable packet ({where, decisions, work, next}) instead of the six-line text summary.

commands.name: cells.add
commands.description: Add a cell (or a whole-slice JSON array) from stdin, or from a JSON file. Every cell must declare affects_skills and affects_specs (flat arrays, [] if none). affects_skills holds repo-relative PATHS under skills/ (e.g. "skills/bee-hive/SKILL.md"), never bare skill names — a name is refused here, naming the exact path to use, because the cap-time sync door compares the prediction against touched skills/** paths. Every cell must also declare `role` (model-role-split D7/D8, store 4eaf1b71) — the job this work is, which is what selects the model that runs it — and a cell without a non-empty `role` is refused exactly as one without a `lane` is. Any non-empty name is legal: bee holds no fixed list and membership is NEVER checked, so a new job role needs no new bee code. `code`, `read`, `test`, `docs`, `review`, `design` are the RECOMMENDED vocabulary — authoring guidance carried in the refusal's FIX line, never an enum. A role nothing configures still runs: the dispatch asks for an ordered list headed by the cell's role and falls through to the next name, warning on stderr rather than failing. The purpose of a role is documented where the role is configured: models.<runtime>.<role>.description in .bee/config.json, which the session preamble dispatch-door roles line prints beside the model, so a name bee never invented reaches the next session explained rather than guessed at. Read that table with `bee models show` — it returns every role with its description — and run it before you assign a role if you have not read it this session; never hand-parse .bee/config.json for it, and never pick a name because it sounds right. Cost is a separate lever, never a role — a cell that must run on the session model is escalated with `bee cells escalate`. Prefer --stdin: pipe one cell object or an array for the whole slice in one call — no per-cell scratchpad files. Exactly one of --stdin / --file is required at call time (both satisfy the schema; the handler itself enforces the choice). A batch is validated WHOLE: schema, regen obligations, duplicate ids, and the dependency-cycle check are checked for every cell before any is written, so one call names every problem instead of stopping at the first. --dry-run runs that same whole-batch validation and reports {dry_run:true, ok, cells:[{id, ok, problems}]} without writing anything, clean or dirty — exit 0 when every cell is clean, non-zero otherwise.

commands.name: cells.cap
commands.description: Cap a cell (plumbing — `cells finish` is the porcelain completion verb and wraps this same door). No door runs tests: not cap, not `bee close`, not `bee worktree merge` — they only CHECK the proof line the worker recorded in --report (D7/D8, docs/history/test-doctrine/CONTEXT.md). The worker picks the proof its change type needs (code → related tests; docs → parity/pointer checks; behavior → judge verdict) and records it as "<command> — <result> — <scope reason>"; CI runs the full declared commands.test on every push (rule: agents-proof-at-cap). Small+ lanes still require non-empty --files (what the worker touched); high-risk still requires --outcome; a NEEDS_REVISION judge verdict still refuses without --override-judge; the sync door refuses if touched code in an area skips its owned skill, if a rule home is touched without every applied_at file, or if touched skills differ from affects_skills prediction (escaped with --sync-ack).

Refused when the value is empty or whitespace-only. Repeat calls only keep the last occurrence (the flag parser is single-value, same as every other cells cap/finish flag); pass one line per invocation.

REQUIRED (D8): exactly five keys: outcome (non-empty string), commit (non-empty string), files (array), tests (a proof string "<command> — <result> — <scope reason>", three non-empty segments split on the first two " — " separators, e.g. "cargo test -p bee — green — touched close.rs"; a no-test-sentinel repo names the command segment "none"; a "red" result segment refuses the cap), deviations (array); an unknown or missing key refuses by name, as does a missing --report itself. Stored verbatim to trace.report. Optional sixth key: mistakes (array) — one entry per mistake, each either "<what went wrong> — <what would have been better>" or {wrong, better}; a PRESENT but empty array states that this cell hit none, while an absent key records no answer at all and bee close refuses the feature naming that cell.

mistake.description: One mistake made while doing this cell, in two parts on one line: "<what went wrong> — <what would have been better>", the same " — " separator --deviation and the proof string already use. Write it when you NOTICE the mistake, never composed from memory at the end, and name a concrete noun in the first part — a file, a command, or something you observed. Recorded on trace.mistakes and appended to this run's mailbox, where the run's letter renders it under "Mistakes & reflection". A line missing either part is refused. This is the door `bee cells tier --tier ceiling` used to be: `role` is a cell's sole model selector now, so the three-value cost enum retired and the escalation half of that verb kept its own name. Sets the cell's `escalate` flag, which is what the dispatch reads to run the cell on the session model with no herding command. Refuses when escalating would put MORE than 40% of the feature's cells on the session model (exactly 40% passes — counter-teeth D3, decision 0012) unless --reason names why; the reason is recorded on the cell trace as escalation_reason. --off removes the flag and is never budget-checked.

commands.name: cells.backfill-roles
commands.description: ONE-TIME migration (model-role-split D9/D5, store 4eaf1b71 + 97ce5225): give every stored cell written before `role` existed the role it would have carried, and convert every stored `ceiling` onto the escalation flag. Scans the whole store — the active .bee/cells/*.json path AND .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/ — and maps each roleless cell by the tier it recorded: tier "generation" or no tier at all takes role "code", tier "extraction" takes role "read", tier "ceiling" takes role "code" AND `escalate: true` (the flag the 40% escalation budget and the session-model dispatch both read). Role and flag move in the SAME pass on purpose: the ration divides by a whole-store scan, so a store where some escalations answer the flag and some answer the tier would misreport it. It also carries D4's key rename: a trace still spelling the escalation reason `tier_reason` is renamed in place to `escalation_reason`, value untouched, in the same pass and for the same reason — a half-renamed store answers one question two ways. The `tier` string itself is left in place: D4 retires `tier` as a SELECTOR and does not order stored history rewritten, and a legacy record carrying the field is harmless. Those three things are the only ones this verb writes, and only where they are missing or misspelled, so running it twice changes nothing the second time and an interrupted run is finished by simply running it again. It is not lazy-on-read on purpose: three counters divide by a whole-store scan, so a half-migrated store would misreport every one of them. Counts are computed from the store it is handed — nothing is remembered from the measurement the decision was taken on. Run it with --dry-run first.

dry-run.description: Report the counts — scanned, already carrying a role, what each tier would take, how many escalations would be converted, and how many escalation reasons would be renamed — and write nothing at all. Always the first run.

Cells whose files intersect another session's active reservation hold are skipped (the acting session's own holds never exclude a cell). Claims via the two-store sequence (the claim file first, then the cell record, unwound with a claim-file release on any claimCell throw). Refuses (non-zero exit) when nothing is claimable (NO_APPROVED_WORK), the claims-store race is lost (CLAIMED), or the session's lane binding is broken (LANE_INVALID/LANE_MISSING/LANE_CORRUPT). --session-id is not required at the schema level — omit it and it resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID instead; a session id is still functionally required (claim-next resolves the acting session's own lane from it), so a call with neither still refuses, just from the handler rather than arg validation.

commands.name: cells.reset-budget
commands.description: The ONLY door that reopens a cell whose claim door is closed by CELL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED or REPEATED_FAILURE. Refuses (typed RESET_NOT_NEEDED) unless the cell is actually budget-blocked, and refuses without an actor (--operator, or the BEE_AGENT_NAME env fallback). Requires --reason (audited), logs a decision BEFORE writing the cell (the audit survives even if the write itself fails), and appends {reset_at, reason, by_session, by_actor} to the append-only trace.budget_resets — never rewrites or drops any trace.attempts ledger entry. gate_bypass never substitutes for this: the budget check itself never reads bypass config, so this verb is the only reopening path at any bypass level.

id.description: Cell id whose claim-lifetime budget door is closed.

reason.description: Why a retry is warranted — required, logged to the decision log.

operator.description: Acting operator/agent name, recorded as by_actor in the audit trail and the decision text. Optional — falls back to the BEE_AGENT_NAME environment variable when omitted; refused when neither is present.

session-id.description: Resetting session identity, recorded as by_session. Optional — resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID when omitted.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee cells reset-budget --id demo-1 --reason "manager approved a genuine retry after a real fix" --operator "manager-session" --json

commands.name: cells.dissent
commands.description: Record a dispatched worker's DISAGREEMENT with the cell it was handed: {target, claim, alternative, severity} appended to the target cell's trace.dissent (append-only — an existing record is never overwritten). The severity set is CLOSED: `blocker` and `consider`; any other value refuses by name and writes nothing. At `blocker` severity the target cell is BLOCKED through the same mutation `bee cells block` runs, so every cell that depends on it stops being schedulable while the question is open; a `consider` dissent changes no status at all. --reason (which carries the record's `claim`) and --alternative are free text and are secret-scanned before anything is written, because they are read by a different session. A successful record RELEASES the writing worker's claim — a worker that dissents is exiting, and leaving the claim would make an audited --force-ownership override the routine path for the orchestrator's own verdict. This is NOT `bee cells escalate`, which means model tier and keeps that meaning.

id.description: Cell id the dissent is recorded against — the record's `target`.

reason.description: The dissent's CLAIM: what is wrong with the cell as it was handed to you. Free text, secret-scanned; required and non-blank. Spelled --reason because --claim is a CLI-wide flag-alone boolean (dispatch prepare --claim) and could never carry a value.

alternative.description: What to do instead. Free text, secret-scanned; required and non-blank — a dissent with no alternative is a complaint the orchestrator cannot accept, reject or escalate.

severity.description: `blocker` (pauses the related work: the cell is blocked and its dependents stop being schedulable) or `consider` (recorded and answered, pauses nothing). The set is closed; anything else refuses by name.

session-id.description: Acting session identity, for the claim-ownership guard. Optional — resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID when omitted.

force-ownership.description: Override a live claim owned by a different session (audited).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee cells dissent --id demo-1 --reason "the cell assumes a schema that does not exist" --alternative "add the schema first, in its own cell" --severity blocker --json

commands.name: cells.dissent-verdict
commands.description: The orchestrator's OBLIGATED answer to a worker's dissent (4b7aa303): one of exactly three verdicts, `accept`, `reject` or `escalate`, each with a REQUIRED --reason. The set is closed and exhaustive — anything else refuses by name and writes nothing, and so does an answer with no reasoning, which is the decorative dissent this record exists to prevent. The verdict is written to the DECISION LOG and stamped onto the dissent record (`verdict`, `verdict_reason`, `answered_at`) in one transaction: if the decision-log write fails the dissent stays UNANSWERED and nothing is stamped, because a half-answered dissent that clears a door is worse than no answer. It lands on the OLDEST UNANSWERED dissent, so several dissents take several answers; once every dissent carries a verdict the call refuses — a recorded answer is never overwritten. Any of the three verdicts RELEASES a cell a blocker dissent parked (blocked -> open, dependents schedulable again), because 4b7aa303 obligates an ANSWER and escalate-a-rung is one of the three. `escalate` here means escalate A RUNG — raise the question to the next authority up; it is NOT `bee cells escalate`, which means model tier. This verb takes NO claim-ownership guard: the verdict is the orchestrator's act on a cell a worker dissented against, and a worker-shaped guard would make the audited --force-ownership override the routine path for the ordinary answer.

id.description: Cell id whose dissent is being answered.

verdict.description: `accept` (take the worker's alternative), `reject` (keep the cell as it was handed over) or `escalate` (raise it A RUNG, to the next authority up — never `bee cells escalate`, which means model tier). The set is closed and exhaustive; anything else refuses by name and writes nothing.

reason.description: Why this answer. REQUIRED on all three verdicts, accept included. Free text, secret-scanned, and written verbatim into the decision log beside the claim it answers.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee cells dissent-verdict --id demo-1 --verdict accept --reason "the worker is right: the schema has to land first" --json

commands.name: cells.judge-record
commands.description: Validates a judge-verdict/1 payload (--file) and appends it, stamped with model_independence, to the append-only trace.semantic_judge. Refuses (typed, non-zero exit) on free prose, an unknown verdict/status/fixability/confidence value, or a FAIL check missing failure_signature — never a silent pass. --builder-model/--judge-model (optional) mark that side PINNED for independence derivation: both present AND differing -> "confirmed"; both present AND equal -> "same-model" (honest — the judge still runs); either absent -> "unverified". Never reads .bee/logs/dispatch.jsonl (corroboration only) — the models are caller-supplied from the orchestrator's own pinned dispatch params.

id.description: Cell id the verdict is being recorded against.

file.description: Path to a judge-verdict/1 JSON payload: {schema, verdict, checks[], failure_signature?, fixability, confidence}.

builder-model.description: The resolved model name of the cell's builder dispatch, from the orchestrator's own pinned dispatch param. Omit when not pinned.

judge-model.description: The resolved model name of this judge dispatch, from the orchestrator's own pinned dispatch param. Omit when not pinned.

session-id.description: Recording session identity, for the claim-ownership guard. Optional — resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID when omitted.

force-ownership.description: Override a live claim owned by a different session (audited).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee cells judge-record --id demo-1 --file verdict-demo-1.json --builder-model sonnet --judge-model opus --json

commands.name: cells.schedule
commands.description: Compute the wave schedule for a feature: dep layering + file-overlap serialization, with cycle/unsatisfiable-dep/empty-files diagnostics.

feature.description: Restrict to one feature slug. Omit to schedule every cell.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON (waves + diagnostics) instead of a human-readable report.

commands.name: cells.archive
commands.description: Move a fully-terminal feature's cells (every cell capped or dropped — refuses naming any open/claimed cell) out of the hot .bee/cells/ scan path into .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/, and record its capped/dropped counts in the archive summary ledger so `bee status` reports an honest archived total without scanning the archive tree. Refuses when --feature is the active state.feature (archiving in-flight work is never legal) or when the feature has zero cells. --all-but-active sweeps instead of naming one feature: every feature whose active cells are ALL capped/dropped is archived in one call, the active feature and any feature still holding a live cell are kept and NAMED in `skipped` with the reason. It refuses outright when state.feature is empty — with no resolvable active feature "all but active" would degrade into "all" and archive the in-flight work. Exactly one of --feature / --all-but-active. This is the pressure valve for the hot read path: `bee status` and `bee orient` parse every file in .bee/cells/ on every call, so a repo that never retires finished features pays a growing tax on every orientation.

feature.description: Feature slug to archive — must be fully terminal (all cells capped/dropped) and NOT the active state.feature.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

all-but-active.description: Archive every fully terminal feature except the active one, in a single pass. Mutually exclusive with --feature.

commands.name: cells.unarchive
commands.description: Reverse of cells.archive: moves a feature's cells back from .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/ into the active .bee/cells/ dir and drops that feature's entry from the archive summary ledger. Refuses when the feature has nothing archived.

feature.description: Feature slug to restore from the archive.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: reservations.reserve
commands.description: Reserve a file or glob path for a cell. A conflicting active reservation held by another agent returns ok:false with the holder(s). Optional --session stamps the reservation as owned by that cross-session identity, so the write guard's hold check (checkWrite) can deny another live session's write into the same path — a reservation made without --session keeps today's exact intra-swarm-only semantics. Optional --kind is 'intent' or 'lease' (default 'lease'): 'lease' is a worker's own write-time reservation and stays a hard conflict; 'intent' declares a broad/glob planning-time scope that the write guard only warns about (never hard-blocks) unless it collapses onto the exact write target.

cell.description: Cell id the reservation is for.

path.description: File or directory path to reserve.

session.description: Owning cross-session identity. Omit to keep an intra-swarm-only reservation with no cross-session hold effect.

kind.description: 'intent' or 'lease' (default 'lease'). 'intent' is advisory-only (warn, never hard-block) on overlap; 'lease' is a hard conflict, unchanged from before this flag existed.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee reservations reserve --agent worker-a --cell demo-1 --path src/example.ts --json
bee reservations reserve --agent worker-a --cell demo-1 --path src/example-session.ts --session sess-fsh7 --json
bee reservations reserve --agent planner --cell demo-1 --path "src/api/*" --kind intent --json

commands.name: reservations.release
commands.description: Release an agent's reservations, optionally scoped to one cell.

cell.description: Restrict release to reservations for this cell id.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: reservations.list
commands.description: List reservations, optionally active-only.

active-only.description: Only list reservations not released and not TTL-expired.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line-per-reservation summary.

commands.name: reservations.sweep
commands.description: Release every TTL-expired reservation that was never explicitly released.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: decisions.log
commands.description: Append a decision event to the append-only decision log. Rejects secret-shaped or instruction-like content. Once docs/decisions/taxonomy.json exists, a zero-tag event is refused (typed, names --tags); without that file it warns and proceeds. --relation is required on every call: supersedes:<id>[,...] retires earlier decide/supersede events (resolved against the currently active set, same as decisions supersede's target), touches:<id>[,...] notes a related decision without retiring it, or none when this decision relates to nothing active. A missing or malformed --relation refuses, naming up to 3 conflict candidates and the fix. Decision text that reads as an inline supersession ("supersede(s|d)"/"replaces"/"overrides"/"no longer applies"/"instead of the previous") is refused unless --relation supersedes:<id> names the earlier decision, or `decisions supersede` is used instead. Decision text that reads as a deferral ("defer"/"for now"/"revisit when"/"revisit if"/"later") is refused unless --trigger names a registered trigger (see `triggers add`). --rejected lists the options this decision did not take, one `<what>: <why>` entry each (split like --tags), so the rejected set is a list on the record instead of prose inside --alternatives; omitted, the event carries no rejected field at all. Success output carries a `conflict_candidates` array (up to 3, ranked like `decisions search`'s --text scoring) naming active decisions that share a tag or score >=2 term hits with this one — warn-only, never a refusal; empty when none, plus an `update_obligations` array ([{rule, home, applied_at: [..]}]) listing the applied_at files of homed rules whose area matches a tag or the scope.

tags.description: Comma-separated lowercase slugs (e.g. "billing,nightly-job"), stored on the event for later --tag recall.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

relation.description: Required. supersedes:<id>[,...] | touches:<id>[,...] | none — the decision's relation to prior ones. supersedes: retires the named decide/supersede event(s) from `decisions active`, the same as a `decisions supersede` target; touches: notes a related decision that stays active; none: relates to nothing active.

trigger.description: A registered trigger id (see `triggers add`). Required when the decision text reads as a deferral ("defer"/"for now"/"revisit when"/"revisit if"/"later") — no deferred condition may exist outside the trigger registry.

feature.description: The feature this decision is ABOUT (decision-attribution D2). Outranks the calling session's bound lane, and is how a session charting a discovery effort attributes a decision before that effort has a lane record. Omit it to take the bound lane; an empty value is refused rather than ignored. With neither, the event carries no feature field at all — bee never borrows the shared default state record's feature, because that name belongs to whichever session last made a feature active (D1).

rejected.description: Comma-separated <what>: <why> entries naming the options this decision did NOT take, each with its reason (e.g. "lane-b: doubles the store, buys nothing"). Split exactly like --tags; blank entries are dropped. Omit it and the event carries no rejected field at all — an empty rejected set and no rejected set must not read alike. This is the structured form of what --alternatives says as prose: --alternatives is one sentence a human reads, --rejected is a list a reader can walk option by option.

examples: bee decisions log --decision "Use in-repo registry for CLI commands" --rationale "Avoid duplicated validation logic across dispatcher and hook" --relation none --tags cli,registry --json

commands.name: decisions.supersede
commands.description: Replace an earlier decision with a new one; the earlier decision drops out of the active set. Runs a propagation sweep of docs/** for citations of the superseded id and queues a capture stub per hit. Tag/scope inheritance consults the OVERLAY-APPLIED target, so a legacy target classified only via a retro-tag event still counts as tagged. Once docs/decisions/taxonomy.json exists, the final (explicit-or-inherited) tag set follows the same zero-tag refusal / unknown-tag-accepted rule as `decisions log`.

id.description: Id of the decision being superseded.

rationale.description: Why the replacement supersedes the original.

tags.description: Comma-separated lowercase slugs. Omit to inherit the superseded target's tags.

scope.description: Decision scope. Omit to inherit the superseded target's scope, falling back to "repo" for a metadata-less target.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: decisions.redact
commands.description: Redact a decision from the active set with a reason (the event stays in the log; only its active status changes).

id.description: Id of the decision being redacted.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: decisions.reattribute
commands.description: ONE-TIME correction (decision-attribution D5): fix decisions whose stored `feature` contradicts their own text. bee used to stamp a decision with the calling session's feature and, when that session had no bound lane, fell back to the SHARED default state record - so a decision logged during Discovery took whatever feature another session had made active. Measured 2026-08-25: 23 of the 32 decisions stamped "model-role-split" belonged to human-mailbox or prompt-work-record. The predicate is deliberately narrow: a record is corrected ONLY when its `decision` text opens with `<slug> D<n>` AND that slug differs from the stamped `feature`. A record with no stamp is left unstamped, and a record with no `<slug> D<n>` prefix is left alone - the verb corrects a contradiction the record already carries, it never infers an attribution. Writes ONLY the `feature` field; every other field, and every untouched line, is byte-identical afterwards. Holds the decisions lock across the whole pass, read included, because sibling sessions append to this store continuously. Idempotent - a second run reports zero. Run it with --dry-run first. A targeted pair --id <decision> --to <feature> corrects ONE record by the operator's explicit word - for records whose text makes no claim, which the automatic predicate correctly declines; it refuses to contradict a record whose text claims a different feature.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

dry-run.description: Report what would change - scanned count, corrected count, and each decision id with its old and new feature - and write nothing at all. Always the first run.

id.description: With --to: the one decision to correct, by full id or unique prefix. The pair is the HUMAN-NAMED correction for a record whose text makes no <slug> D<n> claim - the automatic pass correctly declines those. Refuses when the record's own text claims a different feature (that territory belongs to the automatic pass), when the id matches nothing, and always both flags together or neither.

to.description: With --id: the feature slug this decision is about. A stamp already equal to it reports zero changed; only the feature field is ever written.

commands.name: decisions.active
commands.description: List active (non-superseded, non-redacted) decisions, newest first. Optional structured filters narrow the list; --recent applies after filtering.

recent.description: Return only the N most recent (post-filter) active decisions.

scope.description: Exact scope match, case-insensitive (scope is the spec-area dimension).

since.description: ISO date; only events on/after this date (inclusive).

all.description: Also reach events archived by `decisions archive` — a union read of the active store and .bee/decisions-archive.jsonl, de-duplicated by id. Omit for the default active-store-only read.

untagged.description: List only events with no tags AFTER the retro-tag overlay is applied. Composable with every other filter, including --all.

cell.description: Word-boundary text match for a cell id (e.g. "si-1") over decision/rationale/alternatives — a decide event has no structural cell field, so this is a token match, not substring: "si-1" excludes "si-10".

feature.description: Word-boundary text match for a feature slug over decision/rationale/alternatives — same token-match discipline as --cell, not substring.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a formatted list.

commands.name: decisions.search
commands.description: Search active decisions by multi-term text match and/or structured filters. --text is required only when no structured filter (--tag/--scope/--area/--since/--untagged) is given. --text is whitespace-split into terms, case-insensitive, OR across terms, matched over decision/rationale/alternatives AND (overlay-applied) tags — results are ranked by deterministic term-hit count descending, then date descending; a single term matches everything the old substring search matched, and more.

text.description: Whitespace-separated search terms (case-insensitive, OR-matched, ranked by hit count). Optional when a structured filter is present.

scope.description: Exact scope match, case-insensitive (scope is the spec-area dimension).

since.description: ISO date; only events on/after this date (inclusive).

all.description: Also reach events archived by `decisions archive` — a union read of the active store and .bee/decisions-archive.jsonl, de-duplicated by id. Omit for the default active-store-only read.

untagged.description: List only events with no tags AFTER the retro-tag overlay is applied — the classification-completeness check (should reach zero once a backfill is done). Composable with every other filter, including --all; satisfies the "at least one filter" requirement on its own.

cell.description: Word-boundary text match for a cell id (e.g. "si-1") over decision/rationale/alternatives — a decide event has no structural cell field, so this is a token match, not substring: "si-1" excludes "si-10". Satisfies the "at least one filter" requirement on its own.

feature.description: Word-boundary text match for a feature slug over decision/rationale/alternatives — same token-match discipline as --cell, not substring. Satisfies the "at least one filter" requirement on its own.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a formatted list.

commands.name: decisions.archive
commands.description: Move superseded/redacted decision events (always, regardless of age) plus decide events strictly older than --before from .bee/decisions.jsonl to .bee/decisions-archive.jsonl. --before is always required — there is no default age window. Refuses (typed) when zero events qualify. Use `decisions active --all` / `decisions search --all` to keep reaching archived events afterward.

before.description: ISO date. Plain decide events dated strictly before this are archived; superseded/redacted events are archived regardless of this cutoff. Required.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: decisions.tag
commands.description: Append a retro-tag event that overlays tags/scope onto an existing decide/supersede event WITHOUT rewriting its jsonl line — visible via `decisions active`/`decisions search` (including --all) at read time. --target accepts a full id or a unique short8 prefix. --stdin accepts a JSON array of {target, tags, scope?} for a batch: every entry is validated before any write, and one unresolvable target refuses the WHOLE batch (nothing appended). The latest tag event wins when several target the same decision; overlay REPLACES the whole tags array, and scope only when the tag event carries one.

target.description: Full id or short8 prefix of the decide/supersede event to tag. Required unless --stdin is set.

tags.description: Comma-separated lowercase slugs (e.g. "billing,nightly-job"). Required (unless --stdin) — replaces the target's effective tags entirely.

scope.description: Optional scope to overlay onto the target. Omit to leave the target's existing scope untouched.

stdin.description: Read a JSON array of {target, tags, scope?} from stdin for a batch retro-tag (all-or-nothing).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: decisions.render
commands.description: Render docs/decisions/index.md from the active decision store (overlay-aware): grouped by scope then tag (untagged last), newest-first inside each group, one line per decision "short8 · YYYY-MM-DD · first line of decision text". Superseded/redacted events are always excluded; a supersede event renders under its inherited scope/tags. Consumes the SAME overlay-applied read path as `decisions search`/`active`, so a retro-tagged legacy event renders under its overlaid scope/tags, never under "untagged". The file carries a provenance header and is deterministic (byte-identical for the same store) — it is regenerated only, never hand-edited.

all.description: Also reach events archived by `decisions archive` — same union-read flag as `decisions search`/`active`. Omit to render the active store only.

check.description: Read-only: compute the index and compare it byte-for-byte against docs/decisions/index.md on disk, without writing. Exits non-zero (and never writes) when the on-disk file is missing or has drifted (e.g. hand-edited) from what the store would render.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: state.set
commands.description: Set one or more top-level routing fields; only the flags given are written and every other field is preserved. Every call requires explicit --owner equal to the selected default/lane record's valid pre-mutation phase; missing/mismatched ownership or a corrupt phase refuses before write, and a successful phase change rolls ownership forward without persisting an owner field. --phase is validated against the known-phase enum AND against the tail guard: "compounding" is never settable directly (only `state scribing-run` produces it), and "compounding-complete" is legal only from "compounding", only with zero scribing debt, and only with a FRESH recorded compounding run (`state compounding-run`, matching feature, at >= last_scribing_run.at) — --waive-compounding permits the close without one, logging a decision. Every other transition, including all backward moves and --phase idle, stays permissive. Target resolution (symmetric with the read path): explicit --lane <feature> always wins > the calling session's bound lane when --lane is omitted (identity self-resolved at operation moment) > the default state.json for an unbound session. --no-lane forces the default record from a bound session. A missing or corrupt lane — explicit or session-bound — refuses loudly with zero writes, never a silent fall-back to the default. --feature is rejected whenever the selected target is a lane record.

feature.description: Feature slug to set. Rejected together with --lane.

owner.description: Selected record's exact pre-mutation phase. Required for every state set mutation; never persisted.

lane.description: Route the mutation to this lane record instead of the default state.json. Refuses if the lane is missing or corrupt. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically; unbound sessions target the default record.

no-lane.description: Force the default state.json even when the calling session is bound to a lane. Cannot be combined with --lane.

waive-scribing-debt.description: Permit --phase compounding-complete while capped behavior_change cells are still unsynced to docs/specs/. Never silent: it logs a decision naming every waived cell.

waive-compounding.description: Permit --phase compounding-complete without a fresh recorded `state compounding-run` (matching the last scribing run, same feature). Never silent: it logs a decision naming the feature.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state set --lane demo-lane --owner exploring --phase planning --json

commands.name: state.gate
commands.description: Approve or unapprove a named gate, OR pass --merge instead of --name to approve/unapprove the MERGED shape+execution gate in ONE call (sets approved_gates.shape AND approved_gates.execution together, since bee now asks a single Gate 2 question at the end of briefing in place of the separate shape and execution questions). --merge and --name are mutually exclusive. This dedicated command does not accept routing --owner. Idempotent: the same call run twice yields an identical file. Target resolution (symmetric with the read path): explicit --lane <feature> always wins > the calling session's bound lane when --lane is omitted > the default state.json for an unbound session. --no-lane forces the default record. A missing or corrupt lane — explicit or session-bound — refuses loudly with zero writes. A --merge approval inherits the SAME high-risk advisor-consult precondition that already guards a --name execution approval — refuses when mode is high-risk and advisor_ref is missing or stale, before any write. Under --merge, both gates carry the approved_for_plan_rev stamp (a plain --name execution approval still stamps execution alone), so a later `state plan-rev bump` revokes both instead of leaving the merged gate half-revoked. A --merge (or --name execution) approval targeting a LANE also carries D5's plan-time conflict precondition: it refuses when the lane's workflow record carries no conflict_review at all, when the recorded review was derived against a different plan_rev (a `state plan-rev bump` therefore invalidates the review by itself — there is no separate reset, only a fresh `state plan-conflicts derive`), or when any derived candidate still carries no verdict, naming the unverdicted ids. A recorded `conflicts` verdict NEVER refuses: the approval succeeds and names those candidates on a second output line and under `conflicts_acknowledged` on the JSON result, so the contradiction is approved with eyes open. Lane-only — the default (non-lane) record is unaffected, exactly like the advisor precondition.

name.description: Gate name. Required unless --merge is set; refused together with --merge.

merge.description: Approve/unapprove shape AND execution together in this one call, instead of a single named gate. Mutually exclusive with --name.

approved.description: Whether the gate(s) are approved ("true" or "false").

lane.description: Route the mutation to this lane record instead of the default state.json. Refuses if the lane is missing or corrupt. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically; unbound sessions target the default record.

no-lane.description: Force the default state.json even when the calling session is bound to a lane. Cannot be combined with --lane.

owner.description: NOT accepted by this dedicated command — declared here only so the dispatcher's central unknown-flag check still lets it through to this handler's own specific refusal ("--owner is not accepted..."); routing ownership protects generic `state set` fields only.

actor.description: Who is approving — "user" (default) or "auto" for an approval made under gate_bypass. --actor auto requires BOTH --bypass-level and --reason so a bypassed approval is never less traceable than a stopped one.

bypass-level.description: The bypass level under which an --actor auto approval was made, mirroring gate_bypass's own vocabulary. Required when --actor auto is passed.

reason.description: Why an --actor auto approval did not stop for the human gate. Required when --actor auto is passed.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state gate --lane demo-lane --name execution --approved true --json

commands.name: state.waiting-on.set
commands.description: Mark the run as waiting on the human — the agent's own declaration that it asked a gate-shaped or freeform question and is now blocked on an answer (D1: run_state reads "awaiting-approval" from this mark exactly like it does from a pending gate). Writes the mark on the live workflow record when a feature is currently active (the calling session's bound lane, or the default record's own feature) and rebuilds that feature's lane/state projections so `bee status` reflects it immediately; with no feature active, writes the SESSION-SCOPED mark directly on the default .bee/state.json record instead (D3 — a question asked before any feature exists still needs a home). The mark carries --kind, --subject, and the resolved owning session (D4's stale-expiry heartbeat check reclaims against it). It ends three ways, none of them this command: the human's next message clears it automatically, `bee state waiting-on clear` clears it explicitly, or it expires once its own age AND its owning session's heartbeat have both gone stale.

Citation resolution, brief-digest equality and the read-diet check each read a source OUTSIDE the sentence making the claim, and a zero count refuses rather than passing. The digest check resolves every lane's dispatch_id against .bee/logs/dispatch.jsonl, so run this at the root whose log holds the run. When to open lanes at all, and what convergence owes before it logs the decision, live in one place: skills/bee-hive/references/gates-and-delegation.md ("Blind lanes and convergence").

commands.name: supervisor.record
commands.description: Append one supervisor row to the append-only store at the control root (.bee/supervisor/, shared across worktrees). --kind picks the row AND the store. observation and silence go to observations.jsonl and need --note: that file is the memory a COLD tick leaves itself, "looked and chose silence" included, which is a legitimate logged outcome and never an empty tick. intervention, escalation and urgent go to the mailbox interventions.jsonl and need --target-session, --point-key and --question: that row gets a stable id, starts undelivered, and is read by the target session at its next turn boundary. THE FREQUENCY CAP: a second intervention for the same (target session, point key) is refused, and the refusal names its one remedy — record it with --kind escalation, because the same point is never repeated. THE URGENT ALERT: --kind urgent is the danger class. It takes the same fields and the same validation, and differs in exactly two ways — the frequency cap never refuses it (a danger notice is not suppressed by an earlier calm row on the same point), and one best-effort desktop notification fires immediately on a successful write. That notification is fire-and-forget: a missing or failing notifier still leaves the row written and the command green, and the config key supervisor.notify (default enabled) turns it off. Validation happens BEFORE the append: a --kind or --signal outside its closed set, an empty note, a --point-key that is not a slug, a --question of more than two sentences, or a non-numeric --tick refuses and writes nothing at all. The store directory is created on the first write. This verb observes and asks — it dispatches nothing, approves nothing, and writes no other bee record.

kind.description: Row type, closed set. observation (something was seen) and silence (the surfaces were read and no question is warranted) are the tick's own rows; intervention (one open question for one session), escalation (the second pass on a point already raised), urgent (a danger-class alert: never capped, notifies immediately) and advisor-nudge (a recommended advisor consult for the target session, on poor-work evidence — the target's own lead answers it) are mailbox rows.

signal.description: Signal class, closed set: struggling-loop, big-decision, danger-op, budget-overrun, same-region-resubmit, or none. Omitted records as none.

note.description: For an observation or silence row: one or two sentences describing what was observed (500 characters max). Whitespace is collapsed so one record is always one line.

target-session.description: Id of the OBSERVED session. Optional on an observation, REQUIRED on an intervention, escalation or urgent row — a question with no addressee is not a mailbox row. Distinct from --session, which everywhere else names the caller's own session.

tick.description: The control loop's tick index for this observation (non-negative whole number). Omitted when the verb runs outside a loop.

json.description: Emit the written record as machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

point-key.description: Mailbox rows only: a stable slug naming the POINT being touched. Lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, 80 characters max, for example retry-loop-on-auth. This is the key the frequency cap counts, so reuse the same slug for the same point; case and surrounding whitespace never make two points out of one. An urgent row is exempt from the cap but still carries its point key.

question.description: Mailbox rows only: the open question, at most two sentences and 500 characters. It asserts no fault and suggests no answer; longer text, or text shaped like a credential or a control token, is refused rather than delivered into another session's context.

examples: bee supervisor record --kind silence --signal none --note "Read every live session; nothing needs a question this tick." --json

A missing store, or a session with nothing waiting, reads as an empty list rather than an error. One unparseable line warns and is skipped with its line number in unreadable_lines.

commands.name: supervisor.mark-delivered
commands.description: Stamp ONE mailbox row delivered, by the id `bee supervisor pending` printed. The stamp is appended as its own event, so the store stays append-only and the original record is never rewritten. Marking a row that is already delivered is a no-op success that writes nothing and answers changed:false, so a consumer retrying after a dropped response is never punished. An id naming no record is refused, and the refusal names the id.

json.description: Emit the stamped row plus changed as machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: supervisor.away
commands.description: Open a presence window in the store at the control root (.bee/supervisor/presence.jsonl, shared across every checkout of the repo). From there until the window is closed with `bee supervisor back`, every NON-URGENT mailbox row (--kind intervention or escalation) recorded by `bee supervisor record` is stamped queued and takes no immediate path, and the window itself is the span a wake report is later written over. The presence mark has EXACTLY TWO effects and no others (decision 9f5cd250): it defines the report window, and non-urgent supervisor questions queue quietly while it is open. It changes NO gate, no gate-bypass level, no permission or approval path and no waiting-on mark — permission control never hides in a presence flag. Turn-boundary delivery is unaffected as well: a queued row is still listed by `bee supervisor pending` and still read by its target session at the next turn. --kind urgent is untouched — it is never queued and still notifies immediately. Marking away while a window is already open is refused, the refusal names the open window and its remedy, and it writes nothing.

note.description: One line saying where you are or when you are back (500 characters max, whitespace collapsed). It is carried on the window and read back with it.

json.description: Emit the opened window as machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: supervisor.back
commands.description: Close the open presence window and release what queued behind it. The close is appended as its own event, so the store stays append-only, and one release event is appended per queued mailbox row, which clears the queued stamp. The answer carries the closed window's away_at and back_at — the report window — plus the ids it released. The presence mark has EXACTLY TWO effects and no others (decision 9f5cd250): it defines the report window, and non-urgent supervisor questions queue quietly while it is open. It changes NO gate, no gate-bypass level, no permission or approval path and no waiting-on mark — permission control never hides in a presence flag. Turn-boundary delivery is unaffected as well: a queued row is still listed by `bee supervisor pending` and still read by its target session at the next turn. --kind urgent is untouched — it is never queued and still notifies immediately. Closing when no window is open is refused and writes nothing.

json.description: Emit the closed window plus released as machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.description: Read the presence mark: state (present or away), the open window with its id, away_at and note, the last closed window with its away_at/back_at pair, and how many mailbox rows are queued. Read-only — it opens and closes nothing. A missing store reads as present rather than an error, and one unparseable line warns and is skipped with its line number in unreadable_lines.

commands.name: supervisor.report
commands.description: Read the stored WakeReport for one away window — markdown, at most 10 lines, exactly four sections in one order: What happened / What was decided / What needs you / Next action (decision 9f5cd250). READ ONLY: `bee supervisor back` rendered the report once, at the moment it closed the window, and this verb never regenerates it, so two calls answer with the same bytes and neither disagrees with the notification the human already saw. Exactly one report exists per window — the store (.bee/supervisor/reports.jsonl at the control root) is keyed by window id, so a second close can never add a second report. Items inside a section are ordered by impact-if-wrong descending (decision 66c4c251): urgent before escalation before intervention, a gate waiting on you before an ordinary ask, a one-way-door decision before a reversible one. Truncation is part of the shape, not a bug: content that would run past ten lines keeps the highest-impact items and ends with a `+N more` count instead of silently dropping anything. With no --window the newest stored report is answered, and a store with no report yet reads as a plain message rather than an error.

window.description: Id of the away window whose report is read — the id `bee supervisor presence --json` prints for the last closed window. Omitted, the newest stored report is answered; a window with no stored report is a typed refusal.

json.description: Emit report and unreadable_lines as machine-readable JSON instead of printing the report's markdown.

commands.name: supervisor.metrics
commands.description: Read the health counters for one away window — seven numbers, each carrying a TWO-SIDED band, an explicit sample count and a verdict of below-band, in-band, above-band or not-measurable (decision 66c4c251). Every number is DERIVED by the deterministic layer out of records bee already holds: cell files, the decision log, the intervention mailbox and the observation store. Nothing here is model-supplied and nothing is self-reported (decision a8f4b8ab). The seven are escalations per capped cell, blocked rate, wrong-assumption rate (decisions inside the window that a later event superseded), self-answered band (the share of ticks that ended in silence), earned-autonomy streak (consecutive capped cells with zero human-reversed one-way decisions), overrun past 2x a recorded estimate, and same-region repeat (consecutive caps whose files_changed sets are identical). A BAND HAS TWO SIDES: below-band is reported exactly as loudly as above-band, because a supervisor that never speaks is as broken as one that never stops. not-measurable is a first-class verdict and is never rendered as in-band — a counter with no usable input reports nothing, never zero. The overrun counter is skip-until-present (decision ea02cb68): no cell records an estimate today, so it reports the literal state no estimate recorded rather than a guess. With no --window the last CLOSED window is measured; --window names one, open or closed, and an unknown id is a typed refusal. READ ONLY — it writes no store, no config key and no consent level: raising silence-is-consent is EARNED and the human still flips the switch, so the streak is answered as a number and nothing more. The WakeReport carries the same set as exactly ONE of its content lines.

window.description: Id of the away window whose counters are computed — the id `bee supervisor presence --json` prints for the open window and the last closed one. Omitted, the last CLOSED window is measured; an id naming no window is a typed refusal.

json.description: Emit window, counters, out_of_band and not_measurable as machine-readable JSON instead of a formatted list. Each counter carries name, value, samples, band, unit, verdict and state.

commands.name: supervisor.consent-sweep
commands.description: Run the deterministic tick of silence-is-consent (decision c706053e): auto-proceed every queued question that has waited longer than the configured timeout, and say exactly which ones went ahead. OPT-IN AND OFF BY DEFAULT — the mode exists at runtime only when supervisor.consent in .bee/config.json is the record {"enabled": true, "timeout_seconds": <n>} with a timeout of at least one second. Every other read is OFF: a missing key, a non-object, a "truthy" value that is not literally true, a missing or unusable timeout. Consent FAILS CLOSED, unlike supervisor.notify, because a wrong guess here proceeds without the human instead of merely staying quiet. THE SCOPE IS NARROW and each exclusion is refused by name: a gate never takes this path at any setting, and neither does an urgent row, an escalation, an unknown kind, a one-way door asked at low confidence, a row that was never queued behind an away window, or a row already auto-proceeded once. THE TIMEOUT IS DETERMINISTIC: this verb reads one config key and one clock, and no model is ever consulted about whether an ask has waited long enough. EVERY AUTO-PROCEED LEAVES TWO MARKS — the mailbox row is stamped consented_at with the timeout that applied, and one decision is logged in bee's own decision log naming the row, its point key and how long it waited; a row whose decision cannot be written is left queued rather than proceeded. What went ahead is then said out loud: an auto-proceeded row takes the FIRST line of the WakeReport's "What needs you" section, above every other item, and its count rides the report's metrics line. No gate and no gate-bypass level is read or written on this path.

json.description: Emit enabled, timeout_seconds, at, proceeded, proceeded_ids, decisions and skipped as machine-readable JSON instead of a sentence. Each skipped entry carries the row id and the named law that refused it.

With --check, re-renders in memory and byte-compares against disk without writing: any drift (a stale or missing index) exits non-zero naming the file — the same freshness idiom as `bee decisions render --check`.

commands.name: knowledge.context
commands.description: Assemble the budget-aware context manifest for a work item. Resolves --work <id> to the bee.work-item concept whose bee.id matches, then ranks: (1) the work item, (2) its bee.plan sibling in the same work/<id>/ directory, (3) bee.required_context walked TRANSITIVELY in BFS depth order — an already selected path is skipped silently, so a cycle is deduped and never an error, and a dangling or out-of-bundle link is tolerated (OKF §5; grading it is `knowledge check`'s job), (4) the bee.critical: true concepts RANKED BY RELEVANCE to the work item and cut to the pinned keep, (5) every bee.decision concept whose bee.areas overlaps the work item's. The ranked list is then cut at --budget <tokens>: the first entry that would overshoot ends the manifest, and it plus every lower-ranked entry is named in `truncated`. Relevance is the IDF-weighted fraction of a concept's own distinctive vocabulary that the work item's text covers, over title/description/tags and body, plus a small tag/area bonus — chosen by measurement over the live bundle (AUC 0.805 against hand labels; tag overlap alone scored 0.550 and left 48 of 49 patterns tied at zero, so it is disqualified as the signal). The top few criticals are a FLOOR whose cost is reserved out of the budget left after rank 1, so a universal lesson is never evicted by a long required_context chain and the work item is never displaced by its own floor; --budget remains a hard ceiling. Nothing is dropped silently: every critical is accounted for exactly once across `entries` (whose reason names its score and rank), `truncated`, and `excluded` ({path, score, reason}), with `critical_total` stating the population. `zero_signal_count` is always reported, and a real population that is mostly zero FAILS with a typed zero_signal error — a ranking where most items tie at zero is a path sort wearing a relevance label. Ties break by path, so two runs are byte-identical. Sizes are estimated as bytes/4 and the output NAMES that estimator — bee vendors no tokenizer. The output is an ordered MANIFEST — per entry: repo-relative path, bytes, est_tokens, and a one-line inclusion reason — and NEVER file content; the agent decides what to read. `decisions` in the header is informational: the work item's own bee.decisions list, read from its frontmatter, never from a .bee/ store. An unresolvable --work id exits 1 with a typed unknown_work error.

work.description: The work item to assemble context for — matched against bee.id on a bee.work-item concept (the id is identity).

budget.description: Context budget in estimated tokens; sizes are bytes/4 (no tokenizer dependency). Explicit --budget always wins over --lane when both are given.

lane.description: Shorthand mapping to a lane-scaled budget preset (tiny 8000 / small 12000 / standard 20000 / high-risk 30000), resolved into --budget before this call reaches validate() — only when --budget is omitted. Omitting both --budget and --lane behaves exactly as before this option existed (required, missing).

commands.name: knowledge.search
commands.description: Pull matching bee.pattern and bee.area concepts out of the bundle by symptom text — an error excerpt, a wrong-behavior description, a mechanism name — at any moment mid-flow. --text is required, whitespace-split into terms, lowercased, OR-matched by substring containment (the same rule `decisions search --text` uses). The corpus is patterns and areas ONLY: bee.decision concepts are `decisions search`'s (never double-reported), and the generated index.md/log.md files are never concepts to begin with. Matched fields are the concept title, its body (frontmatter stripped), and its frontmatter bee.sources/bee.decisions entries — where incident signatures and quoted error text usually live. Results are ranked deterministically: term-hit count descending, then the concept's own `timestamp` frontmatter field descending, then path ascending, so two runs over the same bundle are byte-identical. Each row is `path — title — why-matched`, where why-matched names every hit term and which field(s) it matched in — a result you can check, not a lucky guess. A zero-hit query is NOT an error: it returns an empty `results` array and a one-line note, exit 0 — a search miss is data mid-debug. Purely read-only: writes is always [], callable from any checkout at any phase.

commands.name: knowledge.promote
commands.description: Propose the knowledge a finished work item earned — and never write it. Resolves --work <id> to its bee.work-item concept, then READS the capped cell traces of that feature from .bee/cells/*.json (a read of the runtime store, which the bundle may perform; it is never a write path into one) and returns three PROPOSALS: (a) a DELIVERY DRAFT — a complete bee.delivery concept in canonical emitter form, ready to be saved as the work item's delivery.md sibling, carrying what shipped (each cell's recorded outcome), how it was verified (each cell's recorded verify command and evidence) and every recorded deviation; (b) AREA UPDATES — for each area named in the work item's bee.areas, the capped behavior_change cells whose files_changed touch that area's subject, as candidate spec-sync bullets each citing its cell id; (c) PATTERN CANDIDATES — every capped cell whose trace carries a deviation or a failure signature, shaped as a candidate bee.pattern concept with bee.polarity pitfall and bee.lifecycle draft, quoting the trace verbatim. Every proposed line traces to a cell trace or to the work item — nothing is invented. promote proposes and never writes — not into docs/knowledge/, not into .bee/*.json(l), not anywhere: `writes` in the --json payload is always []; applying a proposal is a human or agent decision. An unresolvable --work id exits 1 with a typed unknown_work error.

No code scanning in v1 — specs-only import. Two typed refusals, both zero-write: `bundle_exists` when docs/knowledge/ already carries a concept (bootstrap never touches an existing bundle — use `bee knowledge check`/`bee knowledge index` on it instead), and `no_specs` when docs/specs/ is absent or holds no .md files. A spec bootstrap cannot classify (no derivable title, an empty or duplicate slug, or an unreadable file) is skipped and named as a gap rather than failing the whole run; the report names every area CREATED and every GAP so nothing silently vanishes.

commands.name: knowledge.report
commands.description: Read-only recurrence measurement over the bundle's bee.critical patterns. Per U8, an author may add a bee.signature to a critical bee.pattern concept — a deterministic, literally grep-able incident string. For every critical pattern that carries one, this counts the .bee/decisions.jsonl entries (decision/rationale/alternatives text) and .bee/capture-queue.jsonl stub entries (outcome/area/files text, flush rows excluded) whose text contains the signature as a LITERAL substring — never lowercased, never term-split, never OR-matched — AND whose own date is strictly after the pattern's timestamp (compared by calendar day; same-day entries do not count). Each measured pattern renders its recurrence count and last-seen date. A critical pattern with no bee.signature is listed under `unmeasured` and never guessed at. Purely read-only: no write ever reaches a pattern file or either log, callable from any checkout at any phase.

Must be run from the MAIN checkout (an ordinary, non-worktree directory), never from inside another linked worktree. Typed, zero-mutation refusal when the feature slug is invalid, --base-ref does not resolve to a commit, the target sibling path or branch already exists, or a grant already exists for the derived id; `git worktree add` failing at runtime is caught and re-surfaced typed too, and a failure AFTER the worktree was created rolls back best-effort. With `--with-companion`, also runs the project-configured `commands.worktree_companion_start` and symlinks its result into the new worktree at `commands.worktree_companion_mount` — for a nested repo (its own `.git`, gitignored by this one) a bare worktree can't otherwise isolate; bee never assumes what the companion tool is, only that its start command prints JSON `{worktreePath, sessionId?}`. A companion-start failure rolls the whole worktree back, same as any other post-creation failure.

Defaults to the main checkout's current HEAD when omitted.

commands.name: worktree.merge
commands.description: Merge a granted worktree's branch back into the MAIN checkout — first a zero-mutation D7/D8 proof check: every capped cell for the merging feature must already carry a recorded proof line (“<command> — <result> — <scope reason>”, written by `bee cells finish --report`) — `bee worktree merge` never spawns commands.test itself. A capped cell whose report carries no valid proof line refuses the merge outright, naming the cell (WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT); a report-less legacy cap (pre-contract) passes ungated. This check runs before `git merge --no-ff <branch>` is ever attempted (run from MAIN once the check is green), so a proof debt never touches main. Must be run from the MAIN checkout (an ordinary, non-worktree directory) — running it from inside ANY linked worktree, including the one being merged, is refused (a worktree cannot merge itself). Typed, zero-mutation refusal when the id is unknown/ungranted, the MAIN or WORKTREE tree is dirty (a bootstrapped gitignored .bee store alone does not count as dirty), or the worktree is on a detached HEAD or a branch other than its expected `wt/<slug>`-style branch. Cleanup runs BY DEFAULT on a green (or skipped, loudly-warned) merge that actually merged something: `git worktree remove --force` (safe only because freshness was re-checked immediately before), `git branch -d` (never -D), then removeGrant — so a merged id never lingers in `bee worktree list` unless you ask it to. Pass `--no-cleanup` to opt ONE merge out, or set `.bee/config.json`'s `worktree_cleanup_on_merge` to `false` to opt a whole repo out; a non-boolean value on either is refused outright, never silently read as on. The legacy `--cleanup` flag is still accepted and validated but is now a no-op — cleanup-by-default replaced its old opt-in meaning, so passing it changes nothing. Cleanup never runs when the merge itself came back MERGE_CONFLICT or WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT, or when nothing was actually merged (an already-up-to-date branch removes nothing, flag or config notwithstanding). No flag needed for companion teardown: if the worktree was created `--with-companion`, its marker alone is enough — commands.worktree_companion_end runs and the mounted symlink is removed BEFORE the dirty-tree check, regardless of cleanup or how the merge itself resolves (an untracked companion symlink would otherwise read as a dirty worktree on every attempt). Queue-aware: every invocation enqueues through the shared integration queue (`controlRoot/.bee/runtime/integration/queue/`) and becomes the processor the instant the lease is free — an empty queue resolves immediately with the same output as an uncontended merge. A second concurrent merge against the same MAIN checkout waits its turn (bounded by --queue-wait-ms, default 180000) instead of racing the old dirty-tree refusal; on timeout the result is `ok:false, code:'INTEGRATION_QUEUE_TIMEOUT'` and the text unambiguously says the merge did NOT run, with the request's queue position — never a shape readable as success. uat-gate-before-merge D1: a standard/high-risk feature whose uat gate is not approved refuses the merge outright (zero-mutation, before the companion teardown) unless --skip-uat is passed for this one merge, or .bee/config.json uat_before_merge is set to false — the remedy names all three exits. Missing or unrecognized lane classification counts as standard (fails closed).

A non-boolean value (anything but a bare flag, `true`, or `false`) is refused outright, never silently read as either outcome. See also `.bee/config.json`'s `worktree_cleanup_on_merge` to opt a whole repo out.

Never combine with an auto-approval — the uat gate itself is never bypass-approved (see bee gate --name uat); this flag only skips the MERGE-TIME check, once, for this invocation. See also .bee/config.json config uat_before_merge (default true) to opt a whole repo out.

Every probe fails CLOSED: a missing record, an unreadable file, or a non-zero git exit keeps the worktree rather than removing it, and an unresolvable base ref refuses the whole run. Drops all four artifacts per dead worktree: directory (git worktree remove --force), branch (git branch -d, never -D), grant, workspace record, and prints one line per worktree naming why it was kept or removed; a removal line names the bytes reclaimed. Must be run from the MAIN checkout: it enumerates and removes OTHER worktrees, so a linked worktree cannot prune itself. Lock a worktree with git worktree lock <path> to opt it out permanently, git worktree remove --force refuses outright on a locked tree.
