commands.name: dispatch.prepare
commands.description: Build a bee-owned dispatch payload (Agent tool / spawn_agent / an external cli executor) for the given runtime and purpose, plus an economics record (logical_tier, requested_model, channel, enforcement). kind "cell" resolves the cell-role-headed ordered list — [<cell role>, "code", "generation"], read cells via ["read", "extraction", "generation"] — and requires --cell (loaded for prompt context) and --worker (checked against the cell's own status/claim owner); kind "gather" stays the read-only default (extraction-headed for a --role extraction ask), kind "reviewer" resolves the review role falling through to generation; kind "advisor" resolves the configured advisor slot alone — one name, no fall-through. --role <name> overrides the slot the kind would have resolved, so any configured role is reachable through this one door without a new kind. A cli-shaped resolution for kind "cell" is returned as a typed refusal ({ok:false, reason:"cli_tier_gather_only", ...}) — prepare never routes around it. For kind "cell", an unclaimed or foreign-claimed cell is refused as {ok:false, type:"refused", reason:"claim_ownership", code, status, owner, fix} naming the actual status/owner — --force-ownership overrides it and appends an audited ownership_override entry to the prepare-time dispatch record. A cli-shaped resolution for gather/reviewer/advisor builds an external-executor Bash payload instead of an Agent/spawn_agent one. Prompt wording lives in the vendored prompts/*.md files (rendered through the built-in prompt renderer); for kind "cell", the worker prompt conditionally gains two machine-assembled blocks — a compact "Prior rounds" digest when the cell record carries prior attempt history (blocks, tests-red finishes, deviations, judge consults, reopens), and a "Learned context" block of knowledge paths + one-line titles (never file contents; the cell's own read_first is never duplicated; every resolution failure silent) resolved from the knowledge-bundle work-item manifest, the bundle index pointer, or docs/history/learnings/critical-patterns.md — a first-dispatch cell in a repo with no knowledge layer renders byte-identically to before.

runtime.description: Target runtime the payload is shaped for.

role.description: Role (model slot) to resolve for this dispatch, naming the job the work is rather than the kind it arrives as. Given, it names the slot OUTRIGHT: the kind's default slot is not consulted, and neither is a cell's own recorded value. Any name carried in models.<runtime> is legal (bee holds no fixed list); a name nothing configures is refused as {ok:false, type:"refused", reason:"role_not_configured", role, fix} naming the roles this runtime can resolve. This is how a read-shaped dispatch reaches the cheaper reader: --kind gather --role extraction resolves the extraction slot and returns the bee-extract worker. Omitted, every invocation resolves exactly as it did before the flag existed.

cell.description: Cell id — required when --kind cell; loaded for prompt context.

worker.description: Requesting worker identity — required when --kind cell; checked against the cell's status/trace.worker (claim-ownership guard).

purpose.description: One-line statement of what a non-cell dispatch (gather/reviewer/advisor) is FOR. Folded into the dispatch label as "<kind>: <purpose>" on every transport (the claude Agent description, codex's task_name); ignored for --kind cell, whose label is always "<cell id>: <cell title>". Omitted, the label stays the bare kind — today's exact bytes.

force-ownership.description: Override a claim-ownership refusal for --kind cell (audited into the prepare-time dispatch record). Ignored for every other kind.

claim.description: One verb from "cell chosen" to "worker prompt in hand": claim the cell for --worker first (the same door as `cells claim` — refusals pass through unchanged), then reserve every path in the cell's files for that worker at the default TTL, then build the payload exactly as without the flag. On a reservation conflict the claim is unwound and the refusal names the conflicting paths and holder — state is left as it was found. The result gains {claimed: true, reserved: [paths]}. Only valid with --kind cell.

session-id.description: Session id the --claim claim is taken under (same optional/env-resolved convention as `cells claim`). Ignored without --claim.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of pretty-printed JSON (prepare always prints JSON; flag kept for surface consistency).

expertise.description: Newline-delimited list of '<path> :: <purpose> :: <read-to>' entries describing files or skills the worker should read/load before working. Rendered into the worker prompt's Expertise block.

brief-file.description: Path of a LaneBrief file whose CONTENTS are rendered into the advisor prompt body — the one question a blind lane answers, carried byte-identical across 2-3 parallel advisor dispatches. ADVISOR ONLY: --kind cell is refused ({ok:false, type:"refused", reason:"brief_kind_not_advisor", kind, fix}) because the worker-cell prompt injects learned_context shared across workers, and gather/reviewer are refused by the same arm because their prompts carry no brief block, so a brief passed to them would be swallowed silently. The path is read relative to the current working directory; the file is capped at 8192 bytes (refused as reason:"brief_too_large" naming the cap), must be valid UTF-8 (reason:"brief_not_utf8") and must be readable (reason:"brief_file_unreadable"). The brief is trimmed before it is carried, so a whitespace-only file renders byte-identically to passing no brief at all. When a brief travels, the result and the prepare-time dispatch record both gain brief_sha256 — the sha256 of the carried bytes, so lane-to-lane byte-identity is checkable rather than assumed. Omitted, every payload is byte-identical to before the flag existed.

examples: bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind cell --cell demo-1 --worker exec-demo-1 --json
bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind cell --cell claim-demo-1 --worker exec-claim-demo --claim --json
bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind gather --role extraction --json

commands.name: dispatch.wave
commands.description: Prepare cells of the CURRENT schedule wave (compute_schedule's first placed wave -- the same computation `cells schedule` reads) in one call: each cell runs through the identical claim+reserve+payload path `dispatch prepare --kind cell --claim` uses -- claim, reserve every declared file, build the dispatch envelope -- under an auto-derived worker nickname (`w-<cell id>`), so a payload in `wave` is byte-identical to what the single-cell command would have emitted for that cell. One cell's refusal never aborts the rest: a cell already claimed, or hitting a reservation conflict, lands in `skipped` as `{id, reason, detail}` (`already_claimed`, `reservation_conflict`, `claim_refused`, `prepare_failed`, `unwind_failed`, or `unsupported`) and the loop continues. `economics` carries one `{id, ...}` entry per cell that made it into `wave`. An empty wave (no schedulable cells, or every ready cell already claimed) returns every array empty rather than an absent/null key. This door MUTATES the shared control plane (claims, reservations, worker rows), so it always scopes to exactly ONE feature -- an explicit `--feature`, else the calling session's bound lane, else the default record's own `feature` (the same resolution every mutating `state` verb uses); nothing resolving is a typed refusal, never an every-feature grab. `--limit N` caps how many cells of the wave are actually claimed (the rest are left untouched, not reported); omitted, the whole wave stands.

runtime.description: Target runtime the payloads are shaped for.

feature.description: The one feature this wave scopes to. Omitted, resolved from the calling session's bound lane, then the default record's own `feature`; refused (typed) when none resolves.

limit.description: Maximum number of this wave's cells to actually claim; a positive integer. Omitted, the whole wave is claimed.

session-id.description: Session id every cell's claim in this wave is taken under (same optional/env-resolved convention as `cells claim` / `dispatch prepare --claim`).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of pretty-printed JSON (wave always prints JSON; flag kept for surface consistency).

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Fail-closed runtime health report, a THREE-state verdict: overall_status is "blocked" when any mechanical row (hooks-file presence, capability-baseline byte match, hook-handler resolvability, skills-installed) is not ok; "degraded" when every mechanical row is ok but codex's hook-discovery/trust/project-trust/pending-review rows are still structurally unknown (per the capability matrix) and no valid attestation covers them; "ready" only with mechanical rows all ok AND, on codex, a currently-valid attestation (see "doctor attest") — claude has no trust-unknown rows, so mechanical green alone reaches ready there, no attestation required. Trust-row wording is version-scoped: a live codex --version other than the probed one reports "unprobed_version" instead of asserting the probed conclusions. Never "ready" from file presence alone. Performs zero writes anywhere, including the dispatcher's own pre-routing manifest-hash cache. PORTED 2026-08-02: the 'capability-baseline byte match' row named an artifact that no longer exists in the tree, so it is replaced by the byte match that does — the host's hook manifest against what this binary renders for that runtime. Same question, an artifact that exists, and it fails when it should.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a human-readable report.

commands.name: doctor.attest
commands.description: Record a static attestation that codex trust state was reviewed via the interactive /hooks TUI for THIS exact pairing of .codex/hooks.json content, codex --version, and repo identity. Written to the gitignored .bee/doctor-attest.json (never tracked state). "bee doctor --runtime codex" treats the attestation as valid only while all three legs still match the live state; any single drifted leg makes it inert and doctor reports "degraded" naming the stale reason (hash_changed / version_changed / identity_changed / no_attestation). --runtime codex only — claude has no trust-unknown rows to attest. No liveness leg exists: codex exposes no hook-fire event surface to observe, so this is a static record, not a health probe.

runtime.description: Must be "codex" — claude has no attestation model.

session.description: Optional session id to record alongside the attestation; defaults to $CODEX_SESSION_ID or $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID when unset.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: close
commands.description: Feature close driver — proof-checked: the one blocking door is TESTS, and it never spawns commands.test itself (D7, docs/history/test-doctrine/CONTEXT.md) — it reads whether every capped cell already carries a D8 proof line on its trace.report.tests ("<command> — <result> — <scope reason>", recorded by `bee cells finish --report`): green reports the remaining capture checklist (scribing/capture doors, report-only) and the next action; a capped cell whose report carries no valid proof line exits 1, naming the cell and the remedy — re-cap it with a real proof line, then re-run bee close. A capped cell with no report at all is legacy and passes ungated. --dry-run is a read-only report ({feature, doors:[{door, blocking, detail, command}]}) that runs nothing. Inside a granted worktree the text also names the merge-back road (bee worktree merge — which runs a zero-mutation D7/D8 proof check before `git merge --no-ff`, never commands.test). On a green close the feature's cells are RETIRED automatically: if every one of them is capped or dropped they move to .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/ and leave the hot scan path that `status` and `orient` parse on every call. A feature that closes green while still holding an open cell keeps its cells and close names the cell. Reverse with `bee cells unarchive --feature <f>`; opt a repo out with .bee/config.json `cells_archive_on_close: false`. After a GREEN, non-dry-run close, any dirty .bee/ bookkeeping (retirement, promote proposals) is auto-committed path-scoped to .bee — unrelated dirt and unrelated staged files are never swept, and a commit failure only warns (close stays green); opt a repo out with .bee/config.json `close_commit_bookkeeping: false`.

feature.description: Feature slug to drive toward close.

dry-run.description: Read-only: report the close doors and what settles each, without running anything.

json.description: Emit the machine-readable door report instead of the one-line-per-door text.

commands.name: test
commands.description: Run the project's ONE declared test path — .bee/config.json commands.test (a string or an array, run in order) — and write the normalized record .bee/logs/test-results.json: {ran_at, green, commands:[{command, exit, duration_ms, failure_excerpt, failure_log}]} where failure_excerpt is the last ≤500 chars of a failing command's output (null on pass). The runner is a program; an agent's word is never the record. A red run exits 1 but is a NORMAL result — the record is still written and the red is the next work item (`cells finish` refuses to cap on it). Text output is one ✓/✗ line per command ending in exactly one next: line. No commands.test declared: reports {green: null, undeclared: true} with how to declare it, runs nothing, exits 0.

json.description: Emit the machine-readable run record instead of the per-command text lines.

commands.name: onboard

Idempotent and never destructive: existing state is preserved, and without --apply the call is a read-only PLAN — {status, changes_needed[], versions} — that mutates nothing. A `blocked_*` status means zero mutations happened and the reported `versions` explain why. This is the one maintenance surface every skill points at by name, and it is how a host repo gets the binary the hooks are wired to.

apply.description: Write the planned changes. Without it the call reports what WOULD change and touches nothing.

runtime.description: Which runtime projections to install: claude, codex, or both.

repo-hooks.description: Vendor the hook wiring into the repository.

plugin-source.description: Install from an unpacked plugin package rather than a source checkout.

claude-md.description: Write the CLAUDE.md import that loads the AGENTS.md block.

global-skills.description: Install the skills into the user-level skill directory instead of per-project.

force-downgrade.description: Permit installing an older bee over a newer one.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text form.

commands.name: rs-info

Read-only, needs no repo, and answers "which bee am I actually running" without touching any store.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Print the bee release version — crate::version::BEE_VERSION, parsed at build time from .claude-plugin/plugin.json, the number scripts/release.sh bumps. Text output is exactly `bee <version>`. Rootless and read-only like `bee rs-info`: answers in an empty directory, before onboarding, on a broken store, and touches nothing. The router also serves the conventional spellings `bee --version` and `bee -V` as aliases of this one verb.

commands.name: dev.render-skill-trees
commands.description: Regenerate the plugin skill projections (.claude-plugin/skills, .codex-plugin/skills) from skills/. Run it after ANY skill or reference edit — the projections are committed artifacts, and `bee onboard --apply` copies them, so a skipped render ships the previous wording. Source-checkout tool: it refuses outside a repo carrying both packages/bee/ and packages/bee-rs/.

commands.description: Render one of the vendored prompt files (packages/bee/prompts/*.md) with its placeholders filled, so a prompt change can be inspected before it reaches a worker. Every {{placeholder}} the template declares must be supplied; a missing one is a typed error, never a silently empty slot. Source-checkout tool.

commands.name: dev.statusline
commands.description: Render the one-line bee status line for a host repo's terminal — the surface a runtime's statusLine setting invokes. Read-only, works in any onboarded repo (this is the one dev verb that is NOT source-checkout-only).

commands.name: dev.release-manifest
commands.description: Build, check or self-test the release manifest — the content hash of every file in bee's SHIPPED frame (the gitignored binary appears as a presence-only unhashed artifact). --check reports drift and is what CI runs; --write rewrites the stored manifest, which ADDING a shipped file requires before the rebuild-reproduces-the-committed-manifest test can pass again. Source-checkout tool.

check.description: Compare the tree against the stored manifest and report drift. Writes nothing.

write.description: Rewrite the stored manifest from the current tree.

selftest.description: Run the manifest builder's own consistency checks.

commands.name: dev.plugin-distribution
commands.description: The installers' distribution preflight: prove the client's installed bee plugin package matches the release manifest byte for byte, then plan (and with --apply, perform) the removal of the repo-local fallback copies it supersedes, so two copies of a skill can never disagree. Removal is a transaction — every target is renamed aside first and any failure renames all of them back. Reads a preflight snapshot of every target and revalidates it before touching anything, closing the TOCTOU window between plan and apply. This replaced the last helper script the installers shelled a Node runtime out for. Emits one JSON line; a refusal is {ok:false,status:"blocked",error} with exit 1.

mode.description: plugin-first (prove the package, plan the cleanup) or repo-copy (prove the plugin is NOT active, so onboarding may write repo copies). Required.

repo-root.description: The host repository whose fallback copies are in scope. Required.

release-manifest.description: Path to the release manifest whose package roles define the expected package inventory. Required.

plugin-state-file.description: JSON the installer captured from the client CLI describing its installed plugins, keyed by runtime. A leading UTF-8 BOM is tolerated (PowerShell 5.1 writes one). Required.

apply.description: Perform the planned removal. Without it the run is a dry run that writes nothing and reports what it would do.

codex-hybrid.description: Exempt .codex/hooks.json from the hook cleanup. Set on runs where onboarding just wrote the codex-hybrid hook projection — without it, this pass would strip the only mechanical enforcement Codex sessions get, immediately after the install reported success (GH #22 P0-1).

user-skill-root.description: A user-global skill root to clean, repeatable. Requires --ledger: only skills the ownership ledger names for that exact root are ever touched.

ledger.description: Ownership ledger (schemaVersion 1) naming which skills bee installed under each user-global root. Required whenever --user-skill-root is given.

commands.name: dev.install-support
commands.description: The installer's JSON steps, as verbs rather than inline interpreter one-liners: merge-plugin-state (two per-runtime plugin listings into one {claude,codex} document), plugin-installed (was bee installed for this runtime in the pre-run snapshot — prints 1/0, and 0 for every failure, since 'cannot tell' and 'was not' lead to the same safe rollback), field (one top-level field of a JSON document on stdin, or the literal parse_error), assert-parity (a bee status --json must show installed plus exact version equality and no non-extra drift), and assert-recheck (a fresh onboarding plan must be up_to_date, and names what is still outstanding when it is not). codex.description: merge-plugin-state: the Codex CLI plugin listing.

key.description: field: the top-level key to print.

expect-version-from.description: assert-parity: a plugin.json whose version every projection must equal.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text form.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

commands.name: herding.command-template
commands.description: Print the cockpit's command template for a key — the exact shell line the control loop runs, kept in the binary so the shell scripts hold no command wording of their own.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

commands.name: herding.herdr-result
commands.description: Read a dotted path out of a herdr result document on stdin. Unparseable input is a typed error naming what it received — the control loop must never proceed on a value it failed to read.

context.description: Name used in the error line, so a failure says which read failed.

commands.name: herding.herdr-pane-id
commands.description: Resolve a cockpit pane id from its label, so the control loop addresses panes by name instead of by position.

commands.name: herding.pane
commands.description: The transport-neutral cockpit vocabulary for panes (tmux-herding-cockpit D2): a cockpit role document and bootstrap-cockpit.sh act on panes ONLY through these verbs — never a raw `herdr` or `tmux` line — so a cold control agent reads ONE vocabulary whatever `herding.transport` names. Subverbs: `current` (the caller's own pane, tab and workspace); `list [--workspace ID] [--with-status]` (every pane of one workspace, each row {pane_id, label, tab_id, cwd, command, foreground_cwd, agent_status, agent_session} — `cwd` is where the pane's SHELL started and `foreground_cwd` where its FOREGROUND PROCESS is now, and the anomaly scan reads the second; agent_status/agent_session are advisory and never evidence that work is done); `split <pane_id> [--direction right] [--ratio 0.5] [--cwd PATH]` (result {pane_id}); `run <pane_id> <command>`; `send-text <pane_id> <text>` (refuses a pane classifying Blocked — a dialog is answered by a human, never by whatever character the text starts with); `read <pane_id> [--lines N] [--source NAME]` (result {text}, trimmed to the last N lines); `rename <pane_id> <label>` or `rename <pane_id> --clear`; `close <pane_id>`; `layout [--pane ID]` (result {panes:[{pane_id, width, height, x, y}]}); `tab-create [--label L] [--cwd PATH] [--workspace ID]` (result {pane_id}); `tab-list [--workspace ID]` (result {tabs:[{tab_id, label}]}); `tab-focus <tab_id>`. On tmux (D3) workspace = the caller's session, tab = a window, and label = the pane title. Prints exactly one JSON envelope, identical in shape on both transports: {"ok":true,"transport":"herdr|tmux","result":{...}} and exit 0, or {"ok":false,"transport":...,"error":{"code":...,"message":...}} and exit 1.

main-root.description: Resolve the MAIN checkout root — and therefore the `herding.transport` config key that picks herdr or tmux — against this path instead of discovering it with `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. Accepted by every subverb.

workspace.description: `list`, `tab-list` and `tab-create`: the workspace to act in. Defaults to the caller's own — on tmux the caller's session IS the workspace, so the flag is ignored there.

with-status.description: `list`: fill `agent_status` for every row the transport did not already answer. Free on herdr (its own listing carries the field); on tmux it costs one bounded capture per pane. A pane that will not classify stays null — the flag never turns a readable listing into a failed one.

direction.description: `split`: which side the new pane takes. Default `right`.

ratio.description: `split`: the new pane's share of the split, parsed as a number. Default 0.5; a value that is not a number is a usage error.

cwd.description: `split` and `tab-create`: the working directory the new pane or tab starts in. Defaults to the caller's own current directory.

lines.description: `read`: trim the capture to its last N lines. A whole number; omit for the whole capture.

source.description: `read`: herdr's own source flag. Accepted and IGNORED, so one role line reads the same on both transports.

clear.description: `rename`: drop the pane's label instead of setting one.

pane.description: `layout`: which pane's layout to report. Also accepted as the first positional; with neither, the caller's own pane answers.

label.description: `tab-create`: the new tab's label. Defaults to empty.

commands.name: herding.agent-start
commands.description: `bee herding agent-start <job_id> --kind <kind> --pane <pane_id> -- <args...>` — start one supported interactive agent in an EXISTING pane through the transport-neutral cockpit vocabulary (tmux-herding-cockpit D2), never a raw `herdr` or `tmux` line. The pane must already be sitting at its interactive shell prompt; the transport is the one `herding.transport` names. Everything after a bare `--` is the agent's OWN argv and is never scanned for this verb's flags — not even --main-root — so an agent flag can share a spelling with a bee one. Prints exactly one JSON envelope, identical in shape on both transports: {"ok":true,"transport":"herdr|tmux","result":{...}} and exit 0, or {"ok":false,"transport":...,"error":{"code":...,"message":...}} and exit 1. The transport's own refusal (an unsupported kind, a pane that does not exist) comes back verbatim inside a `transport_error`.

kind.description: The agent kind to start, handed straight to the transport. herdr refuses a kind it does not support; on tmux the kind is the executable the pane execs.

pane.description: The EXISTING pane the agent starts in — it must be at its interactive shell prompt. Split one first with `bee herding pane split`.

main-root.description: Resolve the MAIN checkout root — and therefore the `herding.transport` config key that picks herdr or tmux — against this path instead of discovering it with `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. Must appear BEFORE the bare `--`.

examples: bee herding agent-start demo-job --kind claude --pane w9:p9 --main-root .

commands.name: herding.pane-id
commands.description: `bee herding pane-id --label <label>` — resolve a cockpit pane id from its label, so a role addresses panes by name instead of by position. The transport-neutral twin of `herding herdr-pane-id` (tmux-herding-cockpit D2), and unlike that one — silent, always exit 0, a bootstrap idempotency probe — this is a typed answer a role can branch on: a hit prints {"ok":true,"transport":"herdr|tmux","result":{"pane_id":"..."}} and exits 0, a miss prints an error envelope with code `not_found` and exits 1. On tmux (D3) the label is the pane title, set by `bee herding pane rename` and read back off `list-panes`.

label.description: The pane label to resolve. On tmux this is the pane title.

main-root.description: Resolve the MAIN checkout root — and therefore the `herding.transport` config key that picks herdr or tmux — against this path instead of discovering it with `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`.

commands.name: herding.result
commands.description: `bee herding result <dotted.path>` — read one pane-verb envelope on stdin and print `result.<path>`. Every `bee herding pane`, `agent-start` and `pane-id` call emits exactly one {"ok",...,"transport",...,"result"} envelope, and this is the reader a role pipes it into. The transport-neutral twin of `herding herdr-result` (tmux-herding-cockpit D2), delegating to that verb's OWN reader so the two cannot drift. The walk descends result.<a>.<b>... and stops at null on the first missing hop rather than distinguishing absent from null — the shell callers cannot tell the two apart anyway. Unparseable input is a typed error naming what it received: the control loop must never proceed on a value it failed to read.

context.description: Name used in the error line, so a failure says which read failed. Defaults to `bee herding result`.

commands.name: herding.wave
commands.description: The bee-side entry point (herding-orchestration D17) that turns herding.agent_command into a running wave. Reads herding.agent_command from <main-root>/.bee/config.json, splits token 0 into the herdr agent kind and the remaining tokens into the agent's own argv (D14), substitutes {MODEL} per token, and constructs the fleet crate's HerdrBackend with them — an unrecognised token 0 is a typed error naming the herding.agent_command key, never a generic start failure. Worker specs (name, task, and an optional worktree recorded alongside the row) are read as JSON on stdin: a bare array, or {"workers": [...]}. Runs the fleet choreography and appends exactly one row to the wave ledger (.bee/wave-ledger.jsonl, D10).

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

wave-id.description: The wave ledger row's wave_id. Defaults to a timestamp-based id.

worker-settle-ms.description: Wall-clock ceiling, in milliseconds, the choreography waits for one worker to settle. Default 60000.

poll-interval-ms.description: How often, in milliseconds, the choreography re-reads a worker's status while waiting. Default 500.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

commands.name: herding.occupancy
commands.description: The CLI bridge to the wave ledger's read side (herding-orchestration D10), reachable from a markdown role for the first time — role-dispatch.md §4 can only run shell commands, and the ledger's read side was crate-private. Reports how many worker slots are occupied right now AND which answer it gave: a real cross-check against herdr's own live pane list ("live") when `herdr pane list` succeeds, or the degraded one-hour timer fallback ("fallback") when it does not — the two never collapse into one bare count.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

commands.name: herding.record-worker
commands.description: The recording verb (herding-orchestration D18) role-dispatch.md §8 calls immediately after a successful `herdr agent start`, so the spawn it just made is visible to the very next iteration's `bee herding occupancy` read. Appends exactly one row to the wave ledger (.bee/wave-ledger.jsonl, D10) through the SAME append path `bee herding wave` uses — no second write path, the file stays append-only. The row carries one worker with outcome left unset (null): dispatch spawns and walks away, it never learns an outcome itself. `wave-id` defaults to the worker's own `name` when not given, so a later caller that already knows the same slug can append a resolved row under the identical wave_id and supersede this one at read time (wave_ledger::fold_waves_by_wave_id), never by rewriting these bytes. A spawn this verb is never called for is invisible to the next occupancy read — the whole reason it exists.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

name.description: The spawned worker's own self-chosen slug/label.

pane-id.description: The herdr pane id the worker is running in.

path.description: The worktree path the worker was given, recorded alongside the row.

task.description: The item the worker was given, e.g. a PBI id.

wave-id.description: The wave ledger row's wave_id. Defaults to the worker's own --name.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee herding record-worker --name my-slug --pane-id w4:p9 --path /path/to/worktree --task P-123 --json

commands.name: herding.control-loop
commands.description: The Rust replacement for skills/bee-herding/scripts/control-loop.sh (herding-orchestration D8): a bounded, stoppable poll-act loop that drives one control agent (dispatch or merge), each iteration a fresh headless invocation. Reads the role's opening prompt from skills/bee-herding/references, builds the control agent's argv (D13: byte-identical to the pre-D4 hardcoded default when herding.control_command is absent from .bee/config.json; per-token placeholder substitution, never a shell, when it is present), and runs each iteration under a wall-clock ceiling reproduced without GNU timeout and without a shell — a real terminate signal, then a hard kill after a grace window, sent by pid rather than through the child handle. Checks <main-root>/.bee/tmp/bee-herding.stop both before and after every iteration and exits clean the moment it appears. Counts consecutive failures with a capped backoff and gives up (non-zero exit) at --max-consecutive-failures; stops (zero exit) at the iteration ceiling or on --once. control-loop.sh itself stays in place, unreferenced, until the cell that rewires bootstrap-cockpit.sh removes it.

role.description: dispatch or merge — which control agent this loop drives; selects the prompt file and the --allowedTools surface it is built with.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd. Anchors the stop file so it means the same file bootstrap-cockpit.sh anchors.

timeout.description: Seconds before an iteration is killed and counted as a failed iteration (>=1). Default 900.

max-iterations.description: Stop after N iterations (>=1). Omit for the default cap (10000) — the loop is never unbounded.

max-consecutive-failures.description: Give up (non-zero exit) after N consecutive failed iterations (>=1). Default 20.

turn-ceiling.description: --max-turns passed to the control command's real invocation (>=1). Default 50.

once.description: Run exactly one iteration then exit.

commands.name: herding.run
commands.description: Starts one external CLI agent (any herdr-supported kind) in a fresh pane, hands it a fully self-contained brief over a file mailbox (.bee/mailbox/<job-id>/), and waits for a written result (herding-executor D1/D2/D5/D6/D9). Splits a pane off the caller's own runtime pane, starts the agent via four-step precedence (1: explicit --agent, 2: models.<runtime>.generation when kind: herding with an agent, 3: string herding.agent_command, 4: array herding.agent_command or built-in default; token 0 is the herdr --kind, unchecked — herdr itself refuses an unrecognised kind after the pane split), and polls NATIVELY (zero LLM tokens) for result-N.json, log.txt activity, and herdr agent list status: a stale heartbeat past --idle-timeout or the absolute --ceiling (a hard cap regardless of activity) ends the wait. A well-formed result (done or blocked) closes the pane; a failure or timeout leaves it open as forensics; --close-always closes it on every outcome. Appends one dispatch.jsonl row and one wave-ledger row for every real dispatch. --dry-run renders job.json and the brief without spawning anything. --continue <job-id> reuses an existing job mailbox for a follow-up round instead of spawning a new pane (see the continue parameter). --agent <name> resolves the spawn command through the herding.agents registry by name, overriding both the tier slot and herding.agent_command (see the agent parameter); --continue ignores it.

task.description: The task text handed to the worker, folded into the self-contained brief.

task-file.description: Read the task text from this file instead of --task. A dash (-) reads the whole task text from stdin instead of a real path.

cwd.description: The worker's absolute working directory — the worktree its pane is split into. Defaults to the caller's own current directory.

job-id.description: This job's mailbox identity (.bee/mailbox/<job-id>/). Defaults to a timestamp-based id.

agent.description: Resolve the spawn command by name through the herding.agents registry, overriding both the tier slot and herding.agent_command. An unknown name refuses typed, listing every herding.agents key. Ignored by --continue (the pane already exists).

continue.description: Reuse the EXISTING job mailbox instead of spawning a fresh pane: read the highest prior result-N.json, render round N+1's brief, and send it with herdr agent prompt to the job's recorded pane (persisted into job.json at spawn) — never agent start. Waits on result-(N+1).json under the same --idle-timeout/--ceiling/pane-lifecycle flags. Refuses typed when the job dir is missing, has no prior result, or the recorded pane is gone. --continue --dry-run renders the round N+1 brief and sends nothing. Value is the job id to continue.

idle-timeout.description: Seconds of no heartbeat (log.txt activity, herdr agent list status) before the wait is declared timed out. Default 900.

ceiling.description: Absolute wall-clock seconds the wait may run regardless of activity — the busy-loop backstop. Default 21600.

close-always.description: Close the pane on every outcome, not only a well-formed result.

main-root.description: Resolve the mailbox, config, and wave ledger against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

dry-run.description: Render job.json and the brief; spawn no pane and no agent.

expertise.description: Newline-delimited list of '<path> :: <purpose> :: <read-to>' entries describing files the worker should read before working. Relative paths join onto worktree_root. Handed into the brief's Expertise section and persisted in job.json for --continue.

examples: bee herding run --dry-run --task "registry smoke test" --job-id registry-smoke --main-root . --json

commands.name: staging.add
commands.description: Merge a feature's branch into the staging mixing-ground (staging-lane D0/D0a): lazily creates the "staging" branch and its sibling worktree (../<repo-basename>--wt--staging) from CURRENT main the first time this runs — never from a feature branch — then resolves --feature's branch (a registered worktree's creation identity, falling back to the "wt/<slug>" convention) and merges it into staging with `git merge --no-ff`. A textual conflict aborts the merge (`git merge --abort`) and reports it typed (STAGING_MERGE_CONFLICT, naming the feature and the conflicting files) — the staged set is left unchanged and staging stays usable for the next feature. On a clean merge the feature is upserted into `.bee/runtime/staging.json`'s `staged[]` (feature, branch, last_merged_sha, at); re-running `add` for the same feature later re-merges (git only replays the new commits) and updates last_merged_sha. Then runs the project's configured commands.staging_build (if any) inside the staging worktree — a non-zero exit is a typed STAGING_BUILD_FAILED error carrying the tail of its output; when commands.staging_build is not configured, the build step is skipped with a visible note, never silently. Must be run from the MAIN checkout (an ordinary, non-worktree directory) — staging is lazily created FROM MAIN and can only ever be triggered from there.

feature.description: The feature slug to merge into staging — resolved to its branch via a registered worktree's creation identity, or the "wt/<slug>" convention.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a short confirmation report.

commands.name: staging.rebuild
commands.description: D0a trigger 3: re-derive the staging invariant (staging = main + Σ features awaiting UAT). Runs `git reset --hard main` in the staging worktree, then recomputes the awaiting-UAT subset of `.bee/runtime/staging.json`'s `staged[]` — a feature whose uat gate reads "approved" on its own workflow record (read from the MAIN root), or whose branch no longer exists, DROPS OUT automatically; missing/unreadable workflow-record state fails toward keeping the feature staged. Every remaining feature is re-merged with `git merge --no-ff`, in staged order, except any named in --without (which stay members of the staged set but are skipped THIS run). A merge conflict aborts just that one merge (`git merge --abort`), is reported typed (STAGING_MERGE_CONFLICT, naming the feature and files) and leaves the feature staged at its last successful merge — one broken feature never blocks re-merging the rest. `base_sha` is updated to main's current commit, then the project's configured commands.staging_build (if any) runs in the staging worktree, same as `staging add`. Must be run from the MAIN checkout; refuses typed (STAGING_NO_RECORD) when no staging record exists yet.

without.description: Comma-separated feature slugs to keep staged but skip merging this run (e.g. "a,b").

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a short confirmation report.

commands.name: staging.status
commands.description: Zero-mutation snapshot of the staging mixing-ground: the current `staged[]` set from `.bee/runtime/staging.json`, each feature's uat gate state ("approved"/"pending"/"unknown", read from its own workflow record on the MAIN root), and a stale-base warning when staging's recorded `base_sha` no longer matches main's current commit — the D0a trigger-3 reminder to run `bee staging rebuild`. Never runs `git reset`, `git merge`, or writes the staging record. Reports `exists:false` (never an error) when no staging record exists yet — `staging status` is a plain query, not a refusal path.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a short text report.

commands.name: discovery.list
commands.description: Scan every discovery effort under docs/discovery/ and report each MAP.md's Destination line plus two ticket counts: open (status: open) and frontier (open, unclaimed, and every blocked-by target closed). An unreadable MAP.md never crashes the scan — it surfaces as a visible "unreadable <path> — remedy: fix or delete" line instead.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the formatted list.

commands.name: discovery.stub
commands.description: Create a new MAP.md for a discovery effort whose destination is not yet known, seeding it with the --from text under Notes. Refuses, writing nothing, when the --effort slug already has a directory under docs/discovery/ — resuming an existing map is a different operation from charting a new one.

effort.description: Lowercase kebab-case slug for the new discovery effort; becomes its directory name under docs/discovery/.

from.description: Prose context seeded into the new MAP.md's Notes section — e.g. why this effort was parked.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee discovery stub --effort onboarding-flow --from "parked from route Qualify: too vague" --json

commands.name: state.plan-conflicts.derive
commands.description: Derive the plan-time conflict candidates for a lane and record them on its workflow record as `conflict_review: {plan_rev, derived_at, candidates}` (D5). Candidates come from two sources, neither of them a new heuristic: every ACTIVE decision the plan's own terms select — the same ranked hints `decisions log` prints, widened to every decision scoring two or more term hits — and every homed knowledge rule whose home or `applied_at` patterns intersect the plan's touched paths. The term set is built from the feature's open and capped cells: their titles plus the stems of every path in `files`, `affects_skills` and `affects_specs`. Each candidate lands with a null verdict; `state plan-conflicts verdict` fills them in one at a time. Re-deriving REPLACES the whole list and therefore clears every verdict already recorded. Zero candidates is a valid derive (an empty list) — and the only state in which "0 conflicts" is a true statement about this plan revision.

lane.description: Route the command to this lane's workflow record. Refuses if the lane is missing/corrupt, or names no live workflow record. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically.

no-lane.description: Force default-record resolution — always refused (conflict_review lives on a lane's workflow record only, exactly like plan_rev). Named so the refusal is explicit rather than a silent fallback.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON (the whole conflict_review object) instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: state.plan-conflicts.verdict
commands.description: Record one derived conflict candidate's verdict on the lane's workflow record (D5). `compatible` means the plan stands beside the prior decision or rule unchanged; `conflicts` means it contradicts it and the contradiction is being taken on with eyes open; `retires-prior` means the plan replaces it — name the prior id in --note. Exactly one candidate is touched per call; every other candidate, and the derived list itself, is left as it stands. An id no candidate carries, or a verdict outside the three values, is refused by name and writes nothing. Emits the whole conflict_review so the caller can see what still lacks a verdict.

id.description: The candidate to record a verdict for — a decision id or a rule id, exactly as `state plan-conflicts derive` listed it.

verdict.description: The verdict to record for that candidate.

note.description: Optional free text stored beside the verdict — the place to name the prior id a `retires-prior` verdict replaces, or why a `conflicts` verdict is being accepted.

lane.description: Route the command to this lane's workflow record. Refuses if the lane is missing/corrupt, or names no live workflow record. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically.

no-lane.description: Force default-record resolution — always refused (conflict_review lives on a lane's workflow record only, exactly like plan_rev). Named so the refusal is explicit rather than a silent fallback.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON (the whole conflict_review object) instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state plan-conflicts verdict --id efd6cbaa --verdict compatible --lane demo-lane --json

commands.name: work.show
commands.description: Show the work record the activity hook opened for this session: the user's own words as the title, the conversation so far, the status, the turn count, and the acceptance once one is set. Emits a null result rather than an error when no record exists — a prompt is what opens one.

session.description: Address this session's record instead of resolving one from the environment. Wins over a herded pane and over CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text rendering.

commands.name: work.set
commands.description: Upgrade the open work record: say what "done" means for the ask (--acceptance), move it along (--status), or both. An acceptance is what promotes a bare prompt stub to a card, so this is the promotion — there is no separate verb. The record must already exist; refuses, writing nothing, when none does, when neither flag is given, when --status is outside open|active|done|dropped, or when --acceptance is empty or matches a secret pattern (an acceptance is the agent's own sentence, so a credential in one is refused rather than redacted).

acceptance.description: What finishing this ask would look like — the sentence a reviewer could check the work against.

status.description: Where the work stands. `open` is the hook's own starting value; the other three are the agent's.

session.description: Address this session's record instead of resolving one from the environment. Wins over a herded pane and over CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text rendering.

examples: bee work set --acceptance "The board names what every live session is working on" --status active

commands.name: models.show
commands.description: Read-only: the whole models role table, exactly as .bee/config.json writes it. Every slot under models.<runtime> is carried through VERBATIM — every shape (a bare model string, {model, effort}, {kind:"cli"}, {kind:"native"}, {kind:"herding"}, even a slot resolution would drop) with its `description` intact, the field the normalized view the dispatcher resolves against strips by design. Roles the config does not name are filled in from that runtime's built-in defaults, and every row carries `source`: "configured" (the config names it) or "default" (bee ships it). A role's MEANING is written down here and nowhere else, and this verb is how it is read — run it before choosing a role for a cell or a dispatch, and never hand-parse .bee/config.json for it. Writes nothing; resolution, the model guard and `dispatch prepare` are untouched.

runtime.description: Show one runtime's table — claude, codex, opencode, or any extra runtime key the config itself names. Omitted: every runtime the config or the built-in defaults know.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text table.

commands.name: mailbox.mark
commands.description: Set the read state bee owns inside ONE filed letter in .bee/human-mailbox. This is the whole surface bee exposes to a consuming inbox: bee owns the letter file and stays its only writer, so the inbox flips read/unread by calling this command and never by editing the markdown itself. The flip goes through the store — read the record, set the one field, re-render, atomic write of the same file — so every other frontmatter field and the whole body come through unchanged. Marking a letter that already carries that status is a no-op success that writes nothing, so a consumer retrying after a dropped response is never punished. An id naming no filed letter is refused, and the refusal names the letter.

id.description: The letter's id: its file name in .bee/human-mailbox (<UTC-timestamp>-<short-run-slug>.md). The .md suffix is optional; answers always name the letter with it.

status.description: The read state to set: "read" or "unread". Any other value is refused — the set is closed and bee owns it.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON ({letter, path, status, previous_status, changed}) instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: mailbox.reflect
commands.description: Write down ONE mistake made during this run, and what would have been better, into the run's human-mailbox entries. The letter filed at the end of the run renders these under a "Mistakes & reflection" section, between "Broken or unfinished" and "Needs your call"; a run that recorded none files a letter with no such section. Call it at the moment a mistake is noticed, or at the run-end look-back — the composing pass only ever renders what is stored here and never authors a reflection of its own. A reflection has TWO required parts and the append is refused when either is missing or empty. It never appears under "Done" and never becomes the letter's subject: a mistake is not a thing the run did, and a letter must not be titled by its mistake. The append is fail-open like every other mailbox entry — a mailbox that cannot be written warns and never turns this into a failure. Call it the MOMENT you notice the mistake, and name a concrete noun in the what-went-wrong part — a file, a command, or something you observed. A run that truly hit none says so with --no-mistakes: that answer is stored, renders in no letter section, and is what bee close's mistakes door accepts in place of a reflection. Silence is not an answer, and close refuses it.

wrong.description: What went wrong, in your own plain words — one sentence. Required unless --no-mistakes is passed; an empty value is refused.

better.description: What would have been better — what you would do instead next time. Required unless --no-mistakes is passed; an empty value is refused.

session-id.description: Which run this reflection belongs to. Resolved the same way every other mailbox stop resolves it: this flag, then BEE_SESSION_ID, then CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, then "unattributed".

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON ({run, kind, at, what, better}) instead of a one-line confirmation.

no-mistakes.description: State that this run hit no mistakes. The other half of the answer: it stores the run's explicit clean-run record, which appears in NO letter section — not "Done", not "Mistakes & reflection" — and never becomes the letter's subject. Refused together with --wrong or --better, which say the opposite. Use it to answer bee close's mistakes door when the work truly hit none.

examples: bee mailbox reflect --wrong "Guessed at the folder name instead of asking" --better "Ask once, up front, before touching anything" --json
